US_day2_plan.purpose: Finish neutralization, not repeat historical merchant massacre.
US_day2_plan.fighter_sweep: roughly 40-55 F6F in the first daylight suppression cycle, followed by mixed strike packages
US_day2_plan.decision: No third full raid day centered once Truk can no longer intervene materially in Catchpole and high-value mobile shipping has already escaped.

day2_air_outcome.dusk_Japanese_attack_recon: 4-7 serviceable, but sortie generation and command network are badly constrained

cumulative_air_losses_raid.note: Branch US losses are materially above historical HAILSTONE because Japanese warning/integration works, but the US retains overwhelming deck and replacement depth.

shipping_closeout.lagoon_additional_day2: 3-5 merchant/auxiliary hulls sunk/constructive-total-loss plus 1-2 small craft; one damaged destroyer may be finished only if unable to move.
shipping_closeout.escape_route_loss: plus one 4,000-7,000 GRT merchant/auxiliary lost to a US submarine during pre-raid evacuation
shipping_closeout.US_surface_gun_kills: No historical Katori/Maikaze-scale surface massacre centered.
shipping_closeout.interpretation: Japan saves most high-value mobile shipping by evacuating early, but not without submarine leakage and abandonment of Truk's fixed logistics base.

fixed_base_damage.airfields: All principal strips repeatedly cratered; emergency operations possible within 24-48h, organized fighter cycles require several days.
fixed_base_damage.radar_plot: roughly 20-35% of pre-raid integrated throughput immediately usable at raid end; enough for local warning, not A-grade full defensive cycle.
fixed_base_damage.precision_AA: 0-1 reliable fire-direction channel immediately after raid; repairable components survive.
fixed_base_damage.supply_immediate_destroyed_or_inaccessib: about 35-50% centered rather than historical ~75-80%, reflecting dispersal and deliberate suppression tradeoffs
fixed_base_damage.workshops_power: major damage; forward carrier/fleet repair role sharply curtailed

human_losses_working.note: Japanese total is much lower than historical mass-ship-loss casualty totals but remains severe due concentrated attacks on airfields, AA, fuel, workshops and remaining vessels.

operational_recovery_clocks.fleet_forward_base_function: NO near-term restoration; high-value tenders/oilers/workshop capability evacuated and fixed infrastructure damaged
operational_recovery_clocks.strategic_role_after_raid: defended air/recon/submarine staging base, no longer a safe Combined Fleet concentration point

reason: Truk unable to mount a major immediate intervention
no need to trade a third day into recovering AA/radar for diminishing returns
US_withdrawal.carrier_state: No additional fleet carrier campaign-out centered; Cabot remains the only pre-existing fast-deck campaign-out casualty from the 3-Feb carrier battle.
US_withdrawal.next: replenish/reorganize while Princeton/Langley/CVEs continue Catchpole support

strategic_judgment.Japan: Avoids historical HAILSTONE catastrophe in ships and transient aircraft, but loses Truk as a practical forward fleet hub and pays heavily in fixed infrastructure and trained local air defense.
strategic_judgment.US: Fails to reproduce the historical destruction ratio, but still achieves the core operational purpose: Truk cannot interfere seriously with Eniwetok and no Combined Fleet concentration remains there.
strategic_judgment.important_branch_difference: The survival of Japanese mobile assets means later Palau/Marianas force wallets are healthier; the absence of an Intrepid night torpedo casualty leaves the US fast-deck wallet healthier too. Both sides carry more mobile strength forward than in the historical HAILSTONE exchange.

next_gate: Close Catchpole/Eniwetok with the resources actually left there, then update Palau/Marianas and Eastern Fleet/Bengal allocation clocks.
